WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON AUGUST 26, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708) WITH FERNANDO ITURRALDE OF LDEQ.

Report Details

Nearest City: Indianapolis / Avon, IN

Medium Affected: AIR

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 39.756399, -86.401400 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** ON 03/04/13 AT 0558 HOURS, TERMINAL TRAINMASTER ADVISED OF AN ODOR AROUND TANK CAR UTLX 910591 (EMPTY LAST CONTAINED PROPYLENE) AT MP QS 9.0 ON THE ST LOUIS LINE SUBDIVISION. THIS IS LOCATED INSIDE AVON YARD IN AVON, INDIANA. THE TANK CAR IS LOCATED ON TRACK 013 IN THE CLASS YARD. CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER WAS NOTIFIED. HENDRICK COUNTY COMMUNICATIONS CENTER WAS NOTIFIED AND ADVISED AVON FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS RESPONDING TO THE YARD. CLEAN UP CONTRACTOR WAS HIRED AND IS ON SCENE. AT 0740 HOURS, FIRE DEPARTMENT ON SCENE WALKING THE TRACKS. AT 0809 HOURS, EFS ADVISED THAT THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT CHECKED THE UTLX 910591 AND DID NOT DETECT ANY ODOR AROUND THE CAR. THEY REPORTED THAT THEY FOUND AN SCMX 4258, LOAD PETROLEUM DISTILLATES, ON TRACK 014 THAT DID HAVE AN ODOR AROUND IT. CONTRACTOR IS ON SITE GETTING INFORMATION AND TRACK PROTECTION. THEY WILL INSPECT THE SCMX 4258 FIRST AND THEN INSPECT THE UTLX 910591. FIRE DEPARTMENT HAS CLEARED THE SCENE. IT WAS FOUND THAT TANK CAR UTLX 910591 WAS HISSING FROM THE TOP.

properties.title: NRC Report: Propylene Glycol in Sanitary Sewer near Park City, UT
properties.summary: Incident Type: PIPELINE - NRC Report ID: 973779 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: DEER VALLEY LUXURY RESORT
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 973779
Incident Time: 2011-04-20 17:30:00
Nearest City: Park City, UT
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: PROPYLENE GLYCOL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: DEER VALLEY LUXURY RESORT
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 1500 gallons
ON WEDNESDAY APRIL 20TH AT APPROXIMATELY 11:30 AM, THE CONDENSER WATER PIPING TO THE COOLING TOWER FAILED AND THE BUILDING LOST MECHANICAL COOLING. THE CONDENSER WATER LOOP WAS FILLED WITH A 20% GLYCOL/80% WATER MIX, THE GLYCOL IS FOR FREEZE PROTECTION. THE GLYCOL PRODUCT IN THE CONDENSER WATER IS PROPYLENE GLYCOL, CAS # 57-55-6 AT A 97% CONCENTRATION AND AN INHIBITOR OF DIPOTASSIUM PHOSPHATE CAS # 7758-11-4 AT A 3% CONCENTRATION. SOME GLYCOL/WATER DRAINED TO THE SANITARY SEWER VIA THE FLOOR SINKS WHERE CCI WAS UNABLE TO CAPTURE THE LEAKS. AGAIN, CCI CANNOT ACCURATELY DETERMINE THE VOLUME BUT ESTIMATE LESS THAN 500 GALLONS WAS LOST FROM THE CONDENSER LOOP IN TOTAL BETWEEN THE FLOOR SINKS AND THE UNDERGROUND SPACE WHERE THE PIPE WAS ROUTED BEHIND THE TOWER BUILDING. THE SNYDERVILLE BASIN WATER RECLAMATION FACILITY HAS BEEN NOTIFIED AND THEY HAVE NO FURTHER REQUIREMENTS OF MONTAGE.

properties.summary: Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN - NRC Report ID: 1058756 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: XCEL ENERGY
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1058756

Nearest City: Georgetown, CO
Location: UNKNOWN SHEEN 5167 GUANELLA PASS RD
Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: XCEL ENERGY
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 39.702006, -105.697582 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 0 gallon
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** DURING AN INTERNAL ENVIRONMENTAL AUDIT ON AUGUST 13, 2013, PSCO DISCOVERED A LIGHT INTERMITTENT SHEEN, SMALL IN AREA, OF LIGHT GREY COLOR, ON THE TAILRACE OF ITS CABIN CREEK HYDRO. GIVEN THE APPEARANCE OF THE SUBSTANCE, THERE WAS SOME QUESTION ABOUT WHETHER IT WAS A NATURALLY-OCCURRING ORGANIC OR PETROLEUM OIL SHEEN. BASED ON A SERIES OF OBSERVATIONS AND BREAK UP TESTS, AND ONCE THE INTERMITTENT SHEEN WAS UNDERSTOOD TO POTENTIALLY BE AN OIL SHEEN, THE SHEEN WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC ON AUGUST 20, 2013 (INCIDENT REPORT #1057719). A SAMPLE WAS TAKEN THE FOLLOWING DAY TO DETERMINE THE NATURE OF THE OIL GIVEN ONGOING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT WHETHER IT WAS ORGANIC IN NATURE. PSCO RECEIVED THE RESULTS OF THE SAMPLING ON AUGUST 26, 2013. ANALYTICAL RESULTS INDICATED THAT THE SUBSTANCE WAS FROM A LUBRICATING OIL AND ADDITIONAL RESEARCH ON OUR END INDICATES IT MAY BE AN EMULSION RESULTING FROM A FEW DROPS OF OIL. THE INTERNAL AUDIT PROCESS, AND THIS NEW DATA, PROMPTED FURTHER REVIEW OF STATION LOGS TO DETERMINE IF ANY OTHER UNUSUAL SHEENS, SIMILAR IN NATURE, MAY HAVE BEEN OBSERVED HISTORICALLY AND WHICH MIGHT POTENTIALLY BE ACTUALLY ONE INTERMITTENT SHEEN. TEN OBSERVATIONS OF HISTORIC LIGHT SHEENS WERE IDENTIFIED AS PART OF THIS INTERNAL AUDIT FROM STATION LOGS AND THE SHEEN OBSERVED DURING THE INTERNAL AUDIT. FROM OCTOBER OF 2012 THROUGH AUGUST OF 2013, DURING DAILY INSPECTIONS, ON NINE DAYS, UNUSUAL SHEENS WERE OBSERVED IN THE TAILRACE OF THE HYDRO PLANT AND LOGGED ON STATION LOGS. IT IS OUR UNDERSTANDING BASED ON CURRENT INFORMATION, THAT THESE LIGHT SHEENS DID NOT EXHIBIT CLASSIC PETROLEUM IRIDESCENCE, LOOKING MORE MUTED IN APPEARANCE. THERE IS NO ANALYTICAL DATA FROM THESE EARLIER OBSERVED SHEENS THAT INDICATES THEY WERE IN FACT FROM OIL. HOWEVER, OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION, WE ARE REPORTING THOSE EARLIER OBSERVATIONS OF WHAT APPEARS TO BE AN INTERMITTENT SHEEN, BASED ON THE NEW INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM THE ONGOING AUDIT INVESTIGATION.

Medium Affected: WATER
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 34.200424, -86.181983 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 8400 gallon
Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1453736/// UPDATED: THERE WAS 8400 GALLONS OF FUEL IN THE STORAGE TANK. SECONDARY CONTAINMENT FAILED, AND THE FRENCH DRAIN AROUND THE CONTAINMENT CAUGHT THE DIESEL FUEL. THE DRAIN WAS CONNECTED WITH STORM RUNOFF. APPROX 4400 GALLONS WAS RECOVERED IN THE STORM DRAINS, RESULTING IN THE REMAINING 4000 GALLONS REACHING THE CREEK. GRAYMAR AND SAFEWAY CONTRACT COMPANIES ARE ON SITE. EPA HAS TWO AGENTS ONSITE, AS WELL AS ADEM. THEY ARE STILL VACUUMING AND CLEANING THE CREEK. THERE WAS ONLY MINOR IMPACT TO GROUND AND THERE IS NO RETENTION POND AS PREVIOUSLY INDICATED. ALL REMANING FIVE TANKS HAVE BEEN DRAINED. (EACH TANK CONTAINING 10,000 GALLONS). IT HAS NOT BEEN DETERMINED IF THERE WILL BE FUTURE USE OF THE SITE. THEY ARE HOPING TO MOVE OUT OF EMERGENCY PHASE, AND THERE IS A MEETING AT 1PM, WHERE A MAINTENANCE PLAN IS BEING DRAWN UP. ORIGINAL REPORTED INFO: THE CALLER IS REPORTING A RELEASE OF DIESEL FUEL ONTO THE GROUND, INTO A RETENTION POND, INTO WET DITCH, AND INTO SLAB CREEK. MATERIAL FROM A 10K GALLON ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK. THE CALLER STATES THAT THERE WAS A BROKEN VALVE ON THE TANK THAT RELEASED ALL THE CONTENTS OF THE TANK. THE SPECIFIC NUMBER OF GALLONS THAT RELEASED IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME.

properties.content:
Report Details

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: R&L CARRIERS
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.664400, -83.559489 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
Report Description
ON DECEMBER 8, 2011, AN R&L CARRIERS TRACTOR TRAILER WAS INVOLVED IN A MULTIPLE VEHICLE ACCIDENT CAUSING BOTH SADDLE TANKS TO BE PUNCTURED, WHICH RESULTED IN A DIESEL FUEL RELEASE ONTO THE SOIL DITCH. THE TRAILER WAS ALSO CARRYING A NON REGULATED LINSEED OIL ON THE TRAILER, WHICH WAS ALSO RELEASED AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT. ERTS DISPATCHED AN ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTOR TO THE SITE TO PERFORM CLEANUP OPERATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR CONTAINED AND SECURE THE AREA OF IMPACTED SOIL AND UTILIZED A VACUUM TRUCK TO COLLECT THE FREE STANDING FUEL/OIL. ON DECEMBER 9, 2011, THE CONTRACTOR RETURNED TO THE SITE AND REPORTED THAT LIGHT SHEEN WAS ON THE DRAINAGE DITCH NEARBY, BUT WAS CONTAINED TO THAT AREA. ABSORBENT BOOMS WERE PLACED ON EACH SIDE OF THE DRAINAGE DITCH TO CONTAIN THE SHEEN AND ABSORBENT PADS WILL BE UTILIZED TO COLLECT THE FUEL.
